This guideline, titled Counseling of Women to Improve Breastfeeding Practices, is the first evidence-informed guideline from WHO for this intervention. It complements other WHO interventions and guidance, such as breastfeeding counseling training courses, integrated infant and young child feeding (IYCF) counseling courses, and tools for community management of at-risk mothers and infants under six months of age. It also aligns with guidelines on optimal feeding of low birth-weight infants in lowand middle-income countries and the Baby-friendly Hospital Initiative. The guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on the optimal timing, frequency, mode, and provider of breastfeeding counseling to improve breastfeeding practices. It is intended for policymakers, technical advisors, and program staff involved in designing and implementing public health programs to support breastfeeding. However, it does not aim to be a comprehensive guide on all potential interventions to protect, promote, and support breastfeeding. For example, it does not address breastfeeding support in maternity facilities, medical contraindications to breastfeeding, community-based practices, peer support, or workplace breastfeeding support. The recommendations in this guideline are based on systematic and narrative reviews of the most recent evidence. It aims to improve the quality and delivery of services to pregnant women and mothers who wish to breastfeed, as well as to enhance monitoring of health system quality by defining expected services and staff competencies. WHO acknowledges the contributions of various departments, technical officers, and external experts in the development of this guideline.
